sensors.name: light sensor RLIGHT (light from above, dim only in a tunnel)

control_flow: driveInTheDark: if RLIGHT is above 75 %, drive forward at 30 %; otherwise call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; otherwise call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left (10/40); otherwise curve right (40/10).

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line; in a dark tunnel without a line, drive straight through without touching its walls; follow the line again after the tunnel.

decision_points.condition: the right light sensor reads above 75 % (bright light)

branches.outcome: no obstacle ahead: follow the line (followLine)

scenarios.coded_response: It drives straight forward at 30 % and never reads the line tracker: in bright light it does not follow the line at all.

scenarios.trigger: The program starts and the light is bright.

assumptions: Following the line means staying on it while the light is bright.

scenarios.coded_response: It checks the obstacle sensor, sees nothing, then follows the line: with no black line it curves right without end, circles, and when a tunnel wall comes directly ahead it stops.
scenarios.initial_condition: Inside a straight dark tunnel, with no black line on the floor and nothing in front of the robot's sensors.
scenarios.trigger: The light sensors read below 75 % inside the tunnel.
scenarios.title: Drives straight through the dark tunnel
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It drives straight through the tunnel without touching the walls.

scenarios.coded_response: In bright light it drives straight forward at 30 % and ignores the line tracker; when the light falls in the tunnel it follows the line for as long as it sees black, then curves right.
scenarios.initial_condition: A black line runs into a dark tunnel; the robot drives in on the line and comes out into bright light onto the line again.
scenarios.trigger: After leaving the tunnel the light is bright again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line again after the tunnel
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line again after the tunnel.

uncertainties: In bright light your program only drives straight and never reads the line tracker, so it does not follow the line there.
In the dark tunnel, with no black line, your program curves right without end and circles into the walls instead of driving straight.
After the tunnel, in bright light, it drives straight again and ignores the line.
In the dark it does read the line tracker, so the line the robot came in on is followed until it is lost, and a line inside the tunnel would be followed.
The program reads only the right light sensor (RLIGHT) and stops only when an obstacle is directly ahead; a tunnel wall that comes in front of the robot's side is not seen by that sensor.
The forever loop re-checks the light many times a second; in bright light it keeps issuing drive-forward, which just keeps the robot driving.
Whether the robot gets out of the dark tunnel at all depends on how it circled, so following the line again after it may not happen in one run.
